author: reek
body: `usb-kbd-hub` puts a full-speed keyboard directly below a high-speed hub, and there the answer is easy: the hub it is plugged into owns the transaction translator, so reading the immediate parent is right. This test puts a FULL-SPEED hub in between. A full-speed hub has no translator of its own -- there is nothing to translate at full speed -- so the keyboard below it is still served by the high-speed hub two tiers up, and the slot context must name THAT hub.

author: reek
body: A walk that reads the translator off the immediate parent finds a full-speed hub, concludes there is no translator, and writes zero. The device then enumerates perfectly, answers every control transfer, and never delivers an interrupt transfer, because the controller declines to schedule a periodic endpoint on a full-speed slot that names no translator. That is the same silent-keyboard shape as the one-tier case, reached by a different mistake, and it is ordinary hardware: a monitor hub in front of a keyboard hub is exactly this topology.

author: reek
body: The root keyboard is unplugged (`-xhci-no-root-kbd`) because the walk takes the first keyboard it finds and the root ports come first.
